questions.q: If the numerator of a fraction be increased by 50% and its denominator be diminished by 28%, the value of the fraction is $\frac{{25}}{{36}}$ Find the original fraction.
questions.s:
Shortcut Trick

Original Fraction = (Resulting Fraction) × (100 − %Decrease in Denom) / (100 + %Increase in Num)

Original Fraction = (25/36) × (72 / 150)

Simplify: (25/150) × (72/36) = (1/6) × 2

Original Fraction = 2/6 = 1/3

∴ The correct option is D.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in Numerator = 50%

Decrease in Denominator = 28%

Resulting Fraction = 25/36

Calculation:

Let the original fraction be x/y.

⇒ New Numerator = x + 50% of x = 1.5x

⇒ New Denominator = y − 28% of y = 0.72y

⇒ According to the question: 1.5x / 0.72y = 25/36

⇒ (x/y) × (150/72) = 25/36

⇒ x/y = (25/36) × (72/150)

⇒ x/y = (25/150) × (72/36)

⇒ x/y = (1/6) × 2

⇒ x/y = 2/6 = 1/3

∴ The correct option is D.

Additional Information

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To increase a value by a%, multiply it by (100+a)/100. To decrease by b%, multiply by (100−b)/100.

Reciprocal Property

When moving a fraction from one side of an equation to another, it is multiplied by its reciprocal: (a/b) × x = c → x = c × (b/a).

Base 100 Method

Assuming the original parts as 100x and 100y simplifies the percentage calculation to 150x and 72y respectively.

Statements:
Some Cats are Dogs.
All Dogs are Rats.
No Rat is a Bat.
Conclusions:
I. No Dog is a Bat.
II. Some Cats are Rats.
questions.s:
(I) Since All Dogs are Rats and No Rat is a Bat, Dogs are completely separated from Bats. So, No Dog is a Bat is True.
(II) Some Cats intersect with Dogs, and All Dogs are inside Rats. So the intersection of Cats and Dogs is also inside Rats. Thus, Some Cats are Rats is True.
Both follow.

questions.q: The price of an article decreased by $8\%$ every year. If the difference between the price at the end of the third and fourth year is $69$, then $40\%$ of the price at the end of the second year is?
questions.s: Dekh bhai, successive ka best logic. End of 3rd year aur 4th year ke price me jo kami aati hai, wo 3rd year ke price ka wahi percentage (8%) hoti hai. Yani $8\%$ of Price(3rd) = 69. Toh Price(3rd) = $\frac{69}{0.08}$. Hame pata hai Price(3rd) = Price(2nd) $\times 0.92$. Isko equate kar: $Price(2nd) = \frac{69}{0.08 \times 0.92}$. Pucha hai $40\%$ yani $0.4$. Toh $0.4 \times \frac{69}{0.08 \times 0.92} = 5 \times \frac{69}{0.92} = 375$.

questions_hin.q_hi: The price of an article decreased by $8\%$ every year. If the difference between the price at the end of the third and fourth year is $69$, then $40\%$ of the price at the end of the second year is?
questions_hin.s_hi: Dekh bhai, successive ka best logic. End of 3rd year aur 4th year ke price me jo kami aati hai, wo 3rd year ke price ka wahi percentage (8%) hoti hai. Yani $8\%$ of Price(3rd) = 69. Toh Price(3rd) = $\frac{69}{0.08}$. Hame pata hai Price(3rd) = Price(2nd) $\times 0.92$. Isko equate kar: $Price(2nd) = \frac{69}{0.08 \times 0.92}$. Pucha hai $40\%$ yani $0.4$. Toh $0.4 \times \frac{69}{0.08 \times 0.92} = 5 \times \frac{69}{0.92} = 375$.
